_sources.discrepancies: NCSL classifies MD as 'no document required' for ID. Maryland has same-day voter registration and early in-person voting. No-excuse mail-in voting is available. Registration deadline is 21 days before the election (online/mail) or same-day in person per MD law. [2026-06-10] Corrected the 2026 primary from July 21 to Tuesday, June 23, 2026 per the Maryland State Board of Elections (early voting June 11-18, 2026; online/mail registration deadline June 2). General election Nov 3 confirmed; general early voting dates (Oct 22-29) are the statutory window - confirm centers with your local board.

earlyVoting.notes: Early voting for the June 23, 2026 gubernatorial primary runs Thursday, June 11 through Thursday, June 18, 2026, 7 a.m.-8 p.m., at any early voting center in your county (Maryland State Board of Elections).

Maryland provides 8 days of early in-person voting, the second Thursday before through the Thursday before Election Day (October 22-29, 2026, per Md. Election Law). Confirm your early voting center: https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/index.html

Maryland offers 8 days of early in-person voting at designated early voting centers (October 22-29, 2026 for the general election). No-excuse mail-in voting is also available. Confirm locations: https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/index.html

votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Maryland does not prohibit phones in polling places. Voters may not photograph their ballot or other voters. Electioneering is prohibited within 100 feet of a polling place entrance.
additionalRules: No document ID required. First-time voters who registered by mail and did not provide ID at registration may need to show ID at the polls.
Closed primary: voters must be registered with a party to vote in that party's primary. Independent/unaffiliated voters may not vote in partisan primaries.
Same-day voter registration available during the early voting period and on Election Day.
No-excuse absentee voting available for all registered voters.

eligibility: Any registered voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason (no-excuse absentee)
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: 7 days before the election online/by mail; 4 days before in person (received by State Board of Elections or local office)
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the local board of elections by 8 p.m. on Election Day, or postmarked by Election Day and received within 10 days after
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must arrive by 8 p.m. on Election Day, or be postmarked by Election Day and received within 10 days after.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Maryland has a closed primary (Md. Election Law §10-201). Only voters registered with a political party may vote in that party's primary. Approximately 1 in 4 Maryland voters is registered unaffiliated and cannot vote in a partisan primary.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Maryland tiene una primaria cerrada (Md. Election Law §10-201). Solo los votantes registrados en un partido político pueden votar en la primaria de ese partido. Aproximadamente 1 de cada 4 votantes de Maryland está registrado sin afiliación y no puede votar en una primaria partidista.
